source.title: Open questions and perspectives for hadron electromagnetic form factors in space-like and time-like regions.

accepted.question_text: Can nucleon electromagnetic form factor models be constructed or identified that reproduce the full set of proton and neutron electric and magnetic form factors in both the space-like scattering region, where the virtual-photon momentum transfer satisfies t = -Q^2 < 0 and the form factors are real functions of Q^2, and the time-like annihilation region e+ + e- ↔ nucleon + antinucleon, where q^2 = -Q^2 > 0 and the form factors are complex?
accepted.context_brief: Unified proton and neutron form-factor models across space-like and time-like regions

evidence.quote: Elastic electron hadron scattering is considered the most direct way to access to FFs, which contain the information on the ground state of the hadron.
In this case, FFs are real functions of one variable, the four momentum squared of the virtual photon, t = −Q2 < 0.
Annihilation processes, as e+ + e− ↔ N + N¯, also give access to the nucleon FFs, but in another kinematical region, where FFs are complex functions of the momentum transfer squared, q2 = −Q2 > 0.
• are there models which can reproduce now all FFs for proton and neutron, in SL and TL regions?

accepted.question_text: Given polarization measurements of elastic electron-proton scattering that show a large deviation of the ratio G_E/G_M from the older dipole-scaling expectation G_E(Q^2) = G_M(Q^2)/μ_p ≃ G_D, what are the consequences for descriptions of light nuclei, such as the deuteron or helium-3, that use nucleon electromagnetic form factors as inputs?
accepted.context_brief: Impact of revised nucleon form factors on light-nucleus descriptions

evidence.quote: They all suggest the following behavior: GE (Q2) = GM (Q2)/µp ≃ GD, GD(Q2) = (1 + Q2[GeV2]/0.71)−2.
The data, not only showed a very large precision, but also a large deviation of the ratio GE/GM from one, expected from Eq. (2).
• what are the consequences of these data for the light nuclei, like deuteron or 3He, which are often described with the help of nucleon FFs?

accepted.question_text: At what momentum-transfer scale do hadron or nucleon electromagnetic form factors reach their asymptotic regime, so that one can test both QCD-inspired asymptotic expectations and the analytic Phragmén-Lindelöf constraint that a form factor has the same limiting value in the space-like limit q^2 → -∞ and in the time-like limit q^2 → +∞?
accepted.context_brief: Onset of asymptotic behavior of electromagnetic form factors

evidence.quote: • when the asymptotic region is reached?
The Phr`agmen-Lindel¨of theorem [22] gives a rigorous prescription for the asymptotic behavior of analytical functions: limq2→−∞ F(SL)(q2) = limq2→∞ F(T L)(q2).
Therefore, the study of FFs at large Q2 represents a unique tool to understanding these properties of the nucleon electrodynamics.

accepted.question_text: Is two-photon exchange in elastic electron-proton scattering responsible for the discrepancy between proton electromagnetic form factors extracted by Rosenbluth separation of unpolarized cross-section data and those extracted by the polarization method from the ratio of longitudinal to transverse recoil-proton polarizations?
accepted.context_brief: Two-photon exchange as an explanation of Rosenbluth-polarization discrepancy

evidence.quote: For the electric proton FF, the discrepancy among the data measured with the Rosenbluth methods (stars) and the polarization method (solid squares) appears clearly in Fig. 1a.
• is the 2γ exchange the reason of the discrepancy between the FFs measured with the two different methods?
All the considerations and results presented above are based on the assumption that the main reaction mechanism is one-photon exchange, the two-photon contribution being suppressed by the order of α.

accepted.question_text: Which experimentally measurable cross sections, polarization components, spin asymmetries, or electron-versus-positron comparisons can identify whether a hadron electromagnetic form-factor measurement is governed by one-photon exchange, two-photon exchange, or their interference?
accepted.context_brief: Observable signatures of the reaction mechanism

evidence.quote: • which are the experiments or the observables which sign the reaction mechanism?
One can conclude that the linearity of the Rosenbluth fit is destroyed by the presence of the two photon mechanism.

The experiment, planned at Novosibirk, is a precise measurement of the difference of electron positron elastic scattering on the proton, which is due only to the 2γ contribution, while the sum contains only 1γ terms (neglecting 2γ terms squared [35].
Other observables sign the presence of 2γ exchange:

accepted.question_text: Does the proton electric form factor G_Ep(Q^2), as inferred from polarization-transfer measurements of the ratio G_Ep/G_Mp, cross zero and become negative at higher momentum transfer, for example in measurements extending the proton form-factor ratio up to Q^2 = 9 GeV^2?
accepted.context_brief: Possible zero crossing of the proton electric form factor

evidence.quote: If the trend indicated by polarization measurements is confirmed at higher Q2 [13], not only the electric and magnetic charge distribution in the nucleus are different and deviate, classically, from an exponential charge distribution, but also the electric FF has a zero and becomes eventually negative.
The extension of the proton FFs ratio measurement up to Q2 =9 GeV2 will show, if the present trend is extrapolated, the presence of a zero in the electric FF.

accepted.question_text: Can time-like-region measurements in e+e− annihilation or proton-antiproton reactions separately determine the electric and magnetic proton and neutron form factors, and can time-like polarization observables such as A_y and A_xz, which contain respectively the imaginary and real parts of G_E G_M*, determine the relative phase between the complex time-like electric and magnetic form factors?
accepted.context_brief: Time-like separation of form factors and phase measurement

evidence.quote: No polarization experiment has been done in TL region.
In TL region, polarization data allow to access the phase of FFs.
In order to determine the relative phase of FFs, in TL region, the interesting observables are Ay, and Axz which contain, respectively, the imaginary and the real part of the product GEG∗M.
But even larger progress is expected in the TL region, where data are scarce and no individual determination of the two nucleon FFs has been done yet.

In particular new data on the neutron are expected in Frascati, as well as polarization experiments which will allow to determine firstly the relative phase between the complex electric and magnetic FFs.

accepted.question_text: Can a complete and sufficiently precise calculation of radiative corrections, including all contributions and interference terms and their effects on electric and magnetic contributions to the reduced cross section, be developed for elastic electron-proton form-factor measurements so that Rosenbluth cross-section extractions and polarization-ratio measurements can be interpreted consistently at large Q^2?
accepted.context_brief: Completeness and precision of radiative corrections

evidence.quote: At large Q2 the Rosenbluth method is not very effective for the extraction of GE, essentially for two reasons: the contribution of the electric term to the cross section becomes very small, as the magnetic part is amplified by the kinematical factor τ, and radiative corrections, which should be applied to the data, can reach 30-40%.

Note that radiative corrections are not applied to the polarization results, as they are assumed to cancel in the polarization ratio [27], although a complete calculation of all contributions and their interference does not exist.
The extraction of GE from the unpolarized data requires a large precision in the calculation of radiative corrections, and in the procedure used to apply to the data.

accepted.question_text: Are nucleon electromagnetic form factors systematically larger in the time-like region than in the space-like region because of a narrow nucleon-antinucleon resonance located just below the nucleon-antinucleon threshold?
accepted.context_brief: Possible subthreshold nucleon-antinucleon resonance explaining time-like form factors

evidence.quote: A possible explanation of the fact that FFs are systematically larger in TL region than in SL region (which is true also in the proton case) is the presence of a narrow resonance in the NN system, just below the NN threshold [19].
